newsitem.title: USA: U.S. June S&P 500s finish lower as techs sell-off.
newsitem.headline: U.S. June S&P 500s finish lower as techs sell-off.

text.p: U.S. June Standard & Poor 500s finished lower as the market was unable to escape from the sell-off in technology stocks, traders and analysts said.
Nasdaq 100s closed sharply lower.
They blamed the weakness in the NASDAQ Composite Index, which is heavily weighted with technology stocks, for June S&Ps' inability to re-test the all-time high of 854.70.
Aside from the declines in bellwether tech stocks, like Intel Corp and International Business Machines, floor traders also pointed to the sell-off in Seagate Technology Inc.
After the market closed Monday, Seagate said its fiscal fourth quarter results would be below expectations due to weak demand for its high-performance computer disks or products.
Last Friday, Intel said its second-quarter earnings would be below expectations and that gross margins would decline from the first quarter's 64 percent.
Intel's CFO Andy Bryant said Tuesday he was "relativity comfortable" with gross profit margins of 60 percent for 1997.
Technically, both Intel and IBM are weak, Jay Hohmann, head of stock index trading at Donaldson, Lukfin & Jenrette Securities, said.
"If Intel drops as much on Wednesday as it did today, it could take out Friday's low," Hohmann said. "These are market leaders, and the way they go could be significant."
June S&Ps attempted several times during Tuesday's choppy session to climb through their all-time high.
"I just have a feeling this market will explode to the upside during June's expiration," one floor analyst said, referring to June's last trading day on Thursday, June 19.
He noted several bullish factors, including September's widening premium against June.
He said the June-September spread widened out to 8.70 points in the afternoon, from 8.30 points in early-morning trade. Late in the day, the spread increased to 8.95 points.
"Stocks are still the best place to put your money," he said, countering talk that asset allocation was continuing after several weeks earlier.
"There are big batches of money from mutual funds and pension investments that have to be put to work," he said.,
While Hohmann believes the market is bullish longer term, he said S&Ps and the NASDAQ may have room to fall. He is estimating cash S&Ps could fall to 800.00 through July.
"We could be talking about a 10-percent drop in the NASDAQ," he said. "There is that possibility."
June's fair value against cash S&Ps is at 1.63 points to cash, with arbitrage buy programs about 2.70 points over and arbitrage sell programs 0.90 over.
June Nikkeis expanded gains after cash Nikkeis closed at their highest level in 1997 overnight.

At the end of pit trade, June S&Ps fell 3.05 at 843.15, new composites lost 0.25 at 441.25, KCBT Value Lines were down 1.70 at 758.00, Nikkeis rose 125 at 20,535, Midcap 400s were off 1.95 at 279.30, Nasdaq 100s were 28.75 lower at 930.00 and Russell 2000s were down 2.95 at 381.75.
